source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work uses higher-order-cumulant rank matrices for source and effect estimation in latent-confounded linear non-Gaussian models; it is a bivariate loading-recovery comparator, not a complete ternary beta-fiber frontier.

The paper develops computer-algebra tests for identifiable, generically identifiable, and non-generically-identifiable causal effects in linear SEMs; it does not classify this proxy model's real truncated-moment fibers.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Proceedings abstract; Theorem 3.8 text verified from the public paper search result.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives a complete graphical characterization of identifiable direct and total effects in lvLiNGAM with known or unknown graph, based on full-law overcomplete-ICA reasoning rather than a finite cumulant-depth frontier.

The paper gives an if-and-only-if characterization of overcomplete ICA mixing identifiability and a recovery algorithm; it is a full-distribution mixing result rather than a finite truncated-cumulant beta-depth theorem.
The paper identifies effects from a single proxy under a known proxy-generation mechanism and a completeness condition, so it does not subsume the unknown-mechanism non-Gaussian graph.
The article develops identification- and singularity-robust tests for general linear and nonlinear moment-condition models, not the proposal's quantified legal proxy-cumulant fiber.
The paper uses test inversion to construct total-effect confidence regions accounting for causal-structure uncertainty, in a different bivariate linear-model setting.
